title: A starry combination
caption: The Auxiliary Telescopes under the Magellanic Clouds, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The four Auxiliary Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope stand against a sky thick with stars on Cerro Paranal. Hanging above the site are the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds, two objects that can only be seen from the southern sky.

Each Auxiliary Telescope has a mirror 1.8 meters across. Together with the four larger Unit Telescopes, whose mirrors are 8.2 meters across, they make up what ESO calls the world's most advanced optical observatory.

The telescopes can combine their light to form the VLT Interferometer, or VLTI. Working this way, they let astronomers see details up to 25 times finer than a single Unit Telescope can show. The Magellanic Clouds overhead are irregular dwarf galaxies in the Local Group, our galaxy's neighborhood, and they are companions of the Milky Way.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The Magellanic Clouds can be seen by eye from a dark southern site, but a long camera exposure gathers more light and shows many more stars around them.

alt: Four small domed telescopes on a mountain top under a star-filled sky, with two fuzzy patches, the Magellanic Clouds, above them.
